races.title: State House, District 78
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Matt Holway
cands.bio: Retired Democratic nominee for NC House District 78 and longtime Moore County volunteer. Kean University graduate (1980). He has coached high school football, organized charitable events, served as an assistant judge with the Moore County Board of Elections, and mentors with Moore Buddies. Previously registered Republican, then unaffiliated.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Matt Holway was born or raised, or the year he moved to North Carolina. His career before retirement is not described, so his job background could not be assessed. He has not held elected office, so there are no official actions to report. His campaign site has issue pages on schools and vouchers, farms, guns, health care and other topics, but only the Government Priorities page text was available, so we could not report his positions on those. We found nothing on his positions on homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, police pay, or abortion.

local.label: Roots 55: He says he has lived in North Carolina for 40 years and earned a college degree in 1980, so he likely arrived as an adult, but his birthplace and upbringing are not stated.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Listed as retired; his career is not described. He has volunteer experience (assistant judge with the Moore County Board of Elections, high school football coach, charitable event organizer, mentoring volunteer) but no documented elected office or policy or budget career.
qual.why: No paid career or elected office is documented in the sources, so a job-fit score can't be established.
qual.label: Background not found: unknown, not unqualified

stop-data-centers.evidence: Said in his Ballotpedia survey that data centers are a threat to the environment and quality of life, citing strain on water supplies, groundwater and power grids, higher power rates, noise and heat pollution, and few permanent jobs.

clean-money.evidence: Pledged on his campaign site that there will be no corporate or PAC money in his campaign, which he calls grassroots-funded.

second-amendment.evidence: Said Flock automated license plate reader cameras are invasive, violate Fourth Amendment rights, are hackable and have a high error rate. His campaign site frames his position as asking for rules before cameras are allowed. This covers only the Flock camera part of the platform; he has no stated position on gun laws in the pages reviewed.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Called data centers 'a threat to our environment and our quality of life,' citing water and groundwater impacts, massive power demand raising neighbors' rates, noise and thermal pollution, and minimal staffing after construction.

cands.name: Neal Jackson
cands.bio: Republican member of the North Carolina House for District 78 (Randolph and Moore counties) since January 2023. Pastor at Beulah Baptist Church in Bennett since 2009. Earlier ran an insurance and financial planning firm for thirteen years.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Neal Jackson grew up or the exact year he returned to North Carolina. His degrees and the schools he attended are not named in the pages we read. We found no documented actions or stated positions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth and land conservation, immigration and H-1B, police pay, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. His campaign site says only that he has passed legislation on finance, real estate, education and criminal justice, without naming bills. We found no land-use statements, no controversies, and no endorsements for him.

local.label: Roots 40: He was born in Pinehurst, NC, but where he grew up is not stated; the record places him in North Carolina as an adult since at least 2009, when he became pastor in Bennett.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has served in the NC House since 2023, including the Finance Committee. Before that he owned an insurance and financial planning firm for thirteen years and has been a pastor since 2009.
qual.why: Prior legislative service plus a financial-planning business career fits the law and budget job. Committee chairmanships were not counted toward the score.
